conventions.convention: ABC uses a proper prior, standard Borel parameter and data spaces, and a measurable summary into R^d, with d ≥ 1. Tolerance balls are closed and ε ≥ 0.
The tolerance-conditioned target is defined only when its prior-predictive event probability is positive; no quotient is assigned at zero probability.
Rejection proposals are mutually IID prior-simulator pairs indexed from 1; the algorithm returns the first accepted parameter.

The zero-tolerance limit uses a specified jointly measurable nonnegative density version, almost-everywhere continuity at s₀, a single integrable envelope throughout a closed neighborhood, finite positive density evidence, and Countable Choice. It selects a density-based update rather than every RCD version on a null fiber.

Sufficiency requires one parameter-independent conditional-data probability kernel. Posterior preservation is version-wise; pointwise dominated cancellation requires 0 < g(y) < ∞ and finite positive summary evidence. The general theorem assumes AC.

load_bearing.statement: Only when pε(s₀) > 0 define Πε(A | s₀) := M(A × Bε(s₀))/pε(s₀). This is the conditional law of θ under the augmented tolerance event.
For an IID sequence of prior-simulator pairs and p = M(Θ × Bε(s₀)) > 0, the first accepted index is finite almost surely and P(ΘN ∈ A) = M(A × Bε(s₀))/p = Πε(A | s₀) for every A ∈ T.

Under Countable Choice, the specified jointly measurable summary-density version, almost-everywhere continuity at s₀, an integrable local envelope, and 0 < z₀ < ∞ imply total-variation convergence of the positive-tolerance ABC targets to the density-selected summary posterior as ε ↓ 0.

With positive prior-predictive acceptance probability, repeatedly draw fresh independent prior-simulator pairs and return the first parameter whose simulated summary lies in the closed tolerance ball.

concerns.concern: Step 2.1 says 'For measurable A ... and Lebesgue-measurable C ... the ABC definition gives M(A × C)'. The cited definition constructs the summary law on the real Borel space; arbitrary Lebesgue-measurable C requires an explicitly specified extension. The calculations only need Borel intervals, so restricting this assertion to Borel C closes the domain mismatch.
The counterexample uses headings '## Statement' and '## Proof'; SCHEMA.md prescribes '## Statement refuted' and '## Counterexample' for this kind.
The counterexample uses '## Statement' rather than the '## Statement refuted' heading prescribed for counterexamples by SCHEMA.md.

alerts.finding: Step 1.2 states 'The closed ε-ball around 1 is {1/2,1}.' The declared summary target is R and ε = 3/5, so that ball is [2/5,8/5]. Its intersection with the finite data support is {1/2,1}; the subsequent probabilities correctly use this intersection.

The Definition says 'def-likelihood-density selects versions separately for fixed observations'. The cited Definition instead says 'For each θ ... select simultaneously a ... representative pθ', then evaluates those representatives at a fixed observation. Selection is indexed by parameters, not observations. The consumer separately supplies the required measurable fixed-data likelihood, so its target definition remains supported.

seams_checked.note: The prerequisite is contextual. No assigned item imports an optimization theorem or algorithm from that page; the ABC claims do not strengthen its interfaces.

The augmented-target Definition and marginal lemma preserve the proper-prior/kernel setup, closed ε ≥ 0 tolerance event, positive normalizer, and exact tolerance-posterior marginal. They do not identify that marginal with the full-data posterior.

The nonconstant-summary and positive-tolerance examples faithfully apply positive-event ABC conditioning. The rejection citation explicitly retains IID proposals and positive acceptance. The finite-support description of the tolerance ball needs the presentation correction recorded in alerts.
